official_finding.summary: SkyTruth Cerulean's detector logged a 31.17 km, 4.55 km² slick on this scene (model confidence 0.795). A Cerulean human reviewer classed it 'Vessel, coincident', their strongest class, and Cerulean's own record names MMSI 563082600 as the vessel, one of four its scorer considered (best collated source score 0.2598). That MMSI does not appear anywhere in our own scene-time AIS extract for this case. Independent cross-referencing of its IMO (9790634) against VesselTracker, VesselFinder and MarineTraffic (2026-09-12) found the same hull currently broadcasting as MMSI 367337960, name GALVESTON — which is present in our AIS extract and was scored by Stage 3.

official_finding.caveat: This is another algorithm's output with analyst review, not an investigation or a court finding: Cerulean attributed the slick to MMSI 563082600, and nothing here establishes that vessel was responsible. Cerulean's scorer also considered three other MMSIs (368053000, 210145000, 352980797), and the order of that array is not documented as a ranking. No volume was reported. MMSI 563082600 does not appear in our own scene-time AIS extract; an independent IMO cross-check (9790634, 2026-09-12) found the same hull currently broadcasting as MMSI 367337960 (GALVESTON), which does appear in our feed and was scored by Stage 3. That cross-check's stated flag (Singapore) does not match MMSI 367337960's MID (367, which indicates USA) — the Singapore/MID-563 justification in the source note describes the old MMSI, not this one, so the flag is not asserted here. Treat the GALVESTON identity as provisional until the MID/flag discrepancy is resolved.

assessment.explanation: Partial: the corrected record's vessel is in our own scored shortlist, but it is not the one UDGAM ranked first. GALVESTON (367337960) — the MMSI an independent IMO cross-check resolved as the same hull Cerulean's record names — is present in our scene-time AIS extract and was scored 0.650 by Stage 3, closest approach 1.13 km from the origin peak at grid probability 0.943. That is a real, substantial score: on distance and grid probability alone it edges out our own #1 pick, NAGOYA EXPRESS (636093219, 1.30 km, grid probability 0.946), which scored higher only on the aggregate (0.693 vs 0.650, both from 6 of 7 components). So the funnel 48 → 26 → 2 → 2 did surface the corrected vessel and scored it credibly — but the card a viewer would see first, the top-ranked suspect, is NAGOYA EXPRESS, not GALVESTON. Two things this does not resolve: Cerulean's own record still lists a different MMSI (563082600) that never appears in our AIS feed under that number, so either Cerulean's registry lookup and our live scene-time AIS disagree about this hull's MMSI at the time, or these are in fact two different vessels sharing an IMO by coincidence or data error — that has not been independently confirmed beyond the tracker cross-check. And the flag stated for GALVESTON in the cross-check notes (Singapore) does not match its MID (367, USA), which is exactly the kind of detail a judge could check and find wrong if presented uncritically.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: The same age-estimation gap noted before still applies — origin.json's age_method is 'none' on every case, so nothing bounds the rewind by how old the slick actually is. Separately, and specific to this correction: a component that ranks candidates by identity confidence (IMO-verified vs. MMSI-only, cross-registry agreement) would have let GALVESTON's score reflect that its identity was independently corroborated across three trackers, not just its physical placement — right now the scorer has no way to prefer a well-identified vessel over a marginally-better-placed one. And resolving the MMSI 563082600 vs 367337960 question directly — was this Cerulean's registry returning a stale or reused MMSI for the same hull, or a coincidental IMO match — needs one more manual step: pulling the AIS history for IMO 9790634 rather than trusting either source's MMSI in isolation.
